fields.security_summary: NVMe Base 1.4 itself provides only an opaque transport for security protocols via Security Send (Admin OPC 81h) and Security Receive (Admin OPC 82h). It does NOT define a cryptographic stack of its own. Confidentiality and access control are layered above via TCG Opal / Pyrite / Ruby / Enterprise Storage Subsystem Class (SSC) — separate normative specifications that ride on Security Send / Receive. NVMe also defines Sanitize (Admin OPC 84h) for secure data eradication, Namespace Write Protection (FID 84h) for soft / hard / on-power-cycle read-only, and Reservations (NVM Set Specific Command Set) for multi-host coordination. Data integrity on the wire is delegated to PCIe LCRC + ECRC and to End-to-End Data Protection (PI guard + app tag + ref tag).

security_features.name: Security Send / Receive (Admin OPC 81h / 82h)
security_features.type: opaque transport for layered security protocols
security_features.description: Carries arbitrary security protocol commands. SECP=Security Protocol identifier (00h Info, 01h+ vendor); SPSP=Security Protocol Specific. Commonly used to tunnel TCG Opal / Pyrite SP commands.

security_features.name: TCG Opal / Pyrite / Ruby Self-Encrypting Drive (SED)
security_features.description: Layered above Security Send/Receive. Provides a self-encrypting drive with per-LBA-range locking, drive ownership SP, MBR Shadowing, PSID revert, multi-user auth. Defined by Trusted Computing Group; not part of NVMe Base.

security_features.name: Sanitize (Admin OPC 84h)
security_features.description: Three actions: Block Erase (2h), Overwrite (3h, with vendor-defined pattern), Crypto Erase (4h, fast erase via MEK regeneration). Status visible in Sanitize Status log (LID=81h). Cannot be undone.

security_features.name: Namespace Write Protection (Set Features FID 84h, NVMe 1.4)
security_features.description: Four states: No Write Protect, Write Protect, Write Protect Until Power Cycle, Permanent Write Protect. Permanent is OTP — once set, never cleared.

security_features.name: Replay Protected Memory Block (RPMB, Section 8.10)
security_features.description: HMAC-SHA-256-authenticated memory region with monotonic write counter; provides tamper-evident storage for secure boot / DRM use cases. Admin commands NVMe-MI Send (OPC 1Dh) + RPMB messages.

security_features.name: End-to-End Data Protection (PI)
security_features.description: DIF/T10-PI Type 1/2/3: 8 bytes of metadata per LBA carrying 16-bit Guard (CRC) + 16-bit Application Tag + 32-bit Reference Tag. Configurable via Format NVM PI / PIL fields. Detects bit-rot, misdirected writes, and rolled-back writes.

security_features.name: Reservations (NVM Command Set)
security_features.description: Multi-host coordination: hosts register a 64-bit key + acquire a reservation (Write Exclusive / Exclusive Access / Write Exclusive — All Registrants / Exclusive Access — All Registrants); other hosts get SC=0x83 Reservation Conflict on conflicting access.

security_features.name: Lockdown via Lock/Unlock (TCG)
security_features.description: Via TCG Opal Locking SP — Admin SP password locks/unlocks the entire drive at power-on.

fields.no_base_layer_confidentiality: NVMe Base 1.4 does NOT encrypt user data on the bus. PCIe link itself is not encrypted (PCIe IDE — Integrity & Data Encryption — is a separate Gen 5 feature not in Base 1.4). An attacker with bus access (e.g. PCIe interposer) can sniff plaintext. Self-encryption via TCG Opal protects data at rest on media but not in transit over PCIe.
fields.data_integrity_on_wire: PCIe Transaction Layer provides ECRC (32-bit Ethernet CRC) end-to-end TLP integrity; Data Link Layer provides LCRC (16-bit CCITT). Both are wire-error-correction codes, NOT cryptographic MACs.
fields.comparison_to_sibling_emmc: eMMC 5.1 has RPMB (similar to NVMe Section 8.10 RPMB), Secure Erase, Secure Trim. NVMe additionally has Sanitize as a stronger guarantee, NVM Subsystem Reset for forensic-state reset, TCG Opal tunneling via Security Send/Receive (eMMC has no equivalent at the standard layer — TCG-eMMC Opal is rare).
fields.notes: Security requirements at the Base 1.4 layer are limited to (a) opaque tunneling of security protocols via Security Send/Receive, (b) Sanitize for eradication, (c) Namespace Write Protection, (d) Reservations for multi-host coordination, (e) End-to-End Data Protection for integrity, (f) RPMB for authenticated tamper-evident memory. Cryptographic confidentiality (drive self-encryption) is delegated to TCG Opal / Pyrite / Ruby specifications, which ride on Security Send/Receive.
